result.notes:
Added the characterization of the conductor. packages/orch/tests/test_characterization.py runs 11 scenarios on the fake roles: green, red check then correction, finding then triage then correction, quota wait (PROVIDER_WAIT), route fallback (ROUTE_FALLBACK), resume after a stop, INPUT_REBUILT, a blocking question then answer then resume, ad-hoc --input, dynamic review (REVIEW_ADDED) and advisor. Each scenario compares a normalized progress.jsonl and state.json with a snapshot in tests/golden/characterization/<scenario>.json. The normalizer drops ts, duration_s, active_s, wait_s, retry_after_s and the run id. It also masks times, temp/home/project paths, run ids and git/content digests. Tokens stay as the fixtures give them. A snapshot is rewritten only by `python3 tests/test_characterization.py --recapture --reason TEXT`; a run without --reason fails on any difference, and --recapture without a reason exits 2. A coverage test reads the Stops and Beacons tables of docs/conductor.md and requires each code to be in the COVERAGE list, so a new code fails until it is listed. It checks that each listed code is met in the named snapshot or test file. Nine codes that no existing test names (ROLE_OUTPUT_EMPTY, PROVIDER_AUTHZ, CLAIM_BLOCKED, BRIEF_REFUSED, PREPARE_REFUSED, STAGE_SLOW, REPAIR_FAILED, GATE_NOT_WRITTEN, ROLE_LINGERED) got small scenario tests in CodeScenarioTests. Conductor code is unchanged. Tests run: `bash scripts/test.sh -p test_characterization.py` (23 tests) passed in 3 consecutive runs; the snapshots recaptured twice in a row were byte-identical. Acceptance V1 (affected-tests --run) was not run by me.
